Idle my temps are around 40-50 and while playing games it goes to 80-100. I knew this wasn't a good thing so I was gonna wait to buy a good CPU cooler, and get a replacement CPU considering I have a 3 year warranty. I upgraded to Windows 10 and was not having any problems until now, when I play games like CSGO or LoL, I am getting 300+ FPS, that is normal. But for some reason I will get like a huge stutter and my FPS will drop to 30 for like 1 second and come back up. I have been wondering if the CPU is the reason for this and would like some advice on what to do, should I get a replacement CPU and buy a new CPU cooler? Thanks!
PC Stutters on Games and Videos [Help]

http://ark.intel.com/m/products/80807/Intel-Core-i7-4790K-Processor-8M-Cache-up-to-4_40-GHz#@product/specifications

I think it might be a heat issue, seems like the IHS has a tmax of 74 degrees. I'm not sure how far away it is from the cores though, but if I recall it throttles at about 90 degrees for me (i5-3570K).

I'm guessing you've overclocked it? Because those temperatures seem really high otherwise. If not, did you apply thermal paste correctly? How are your fans set up? Those are the only things I can think of, it does seem weird though that it stutters so briefly!

Couple things could be happening here. First if you have thermal paste try going back to the stock cooler and turn off any overclock that you may be running. 100C is way too much for that processor and it will start thermal throttling.

Second 300 FPS is going to be way to much for your monitor and will cause stutter and tearing. Your monitor is most likely only meant to display 60FPS, or 144FPS depending on the monitor. Try turning on vsync in the game to limit the display refresh time, this should help with tearing and with heat.

High cpu temperatures in idle and over 80 degrees (Celsius?) is usually a sign that you did something wrong.

Maybe the thermal paste isn't properly applied?
I agree. OP should get some thermal paste and reapply the heat sink. Those temps are very high, even for the stock cooler.
You could try having the Task Manager Performance tab open and wait for one of the spikes. See what resource is jumping at that time.
